status: PROPOSED — final blocking weights remain an owner decision after the first baseline
purpose: Field-specific trust weighting. Every baseline report must be emitted under BOTH profiles so the weighting choice is visible rather than baked in.

neutral.description: Every field weighted 1. No disposition weighted above another beyond the shared penalty multipliers. This is the control profile.

trust_weighted.description: Proposed profile. An unsupported-certainty error on brand or exact product costs more than an ordinary colour or material miss, because a confident wrong brand is the failure a user acts on and loses money to.

fieldDispositionOverrides._comment: Extra multiplier applied ON TOP of the disposition multiplier, for the specific (field, disposition) pairs where trust impact is disproportionate.

rationale.why_brand_and_exact_product_dominate: A wrong colour is a cosmetic error the user corrects in a second. A confidently wrong brand or exact product sends the user to buy the wrong item. The asymmetry is about consequence, not about how often the field is wrong.
rationale.why_unsupported_certainty_above_incorrec: An 'incorrect' value is a visible mistake the user can catch. 'Unsupported certainty' means the model asserted something the evidence never supported — the user has no signal that it is wrong. Trust erodes on the second kind.
rationale.why_unknown_when_evidence_exists_is_chea: Answering 'unknown' when the label was knowable is a missed opportunity, not a betrayal. It is penalised below an outright error on purpose, so the harness never pressures the model away from honest abstention.
rationale.why_these_exact_numbers_are_not_settled: The magnitudes below are inherited from the Phase 0A disposition model and have NOT been validated against measured data — no baseline has run. They are a starting proposal. Publishing them as final blocking thresholds before a baseline exists would be fabricating a calibration.

reportingRule: A baseline report that presents only one profile is non-compliant. Both profiles must appear, and any metric that changes rank order between profiles must be called out explicitly.
notMeasuredRule: A not_measured disposition carries zero penalty in every profile. It means the metric is out of scope for the contract under test (see MC-1), NOT that the model scored perfectly.
